I did not re-run the work — `registry/item-1` was already `CLAIMED`→`DONE` by me in the previous turn, so re-claiming would have overwritten a completed record and duplicated the artifact. Instead I verified all three sides and confirmed to stew-01 that no re-dispatch is needed.

**Verified state:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `registry/item-1` | `DONE`, assignee `devops-01`, result `s2-item-1-env-manifest.md written` |
| Artifact on disk | Present, 300 bytes, contents intact (heading, four commands + outputs, execution line) |
| Repo HEAD | `f523b11b…` — still matches the SHA recorded in the manifest |

The HEAD match matters: it means the recorded `git rev-parse HEAD` value is still true, so the manifest hasn't gone stale. Captured values were bun `1.3.14`, node `v24.21.0`, `Linux x86_64`.

Two things worth carrying forward:

- The `swarm_memory_get` read anomaly I flagged earlier appears to have been transient — it now returns item-1 correctly. It only surfaced because `list`/`search` agreed with each other while `get` disagreed, so I didn't act on a single failing read path.
- Items 2 and 3 are still `OPEN` and unassigned; prov-01 and ver-01 own those. I noted this to stew-01 rather than reaching for work outside my item.

I'm done — item-1 is closed, the artifact is verified, and no other files were touched.

I'm not done — item-3 is **BLOCKED**, not done.

**What I did:**
- Claimed `registry/item-3` (was OPEN) → CLAIMED
- Read `ROADMAP-V1.md` (169 lines) and extracted F0–F5 from §2 "Frontier ordering"
- Set the item to BLOCKED with an honest result field
- Stored the full extraction at `evidence/item-3-frontiers` so nothing is lost
- Messaged stew-01

**What blocked me:** step 3 requires a `write` tool, but this session has only `read`, `grep`, `glob`, and the `swarm_*` tools. I can't create files.

The extracted frontiers:

| ID | Title |
|---|---|
| F0 | Make the substrate load again (blocking, small) |
| F1 | Close the browser↔chat seam (the real product work) |
| F2 | Prove repeatability, then drift |
| F3 | Second and third provider (Claude, then Gemini) |
| F4 | Single pane of glass |
| F5 | The wider environment |

I deliberately did **not** set status DONE. Doing so would have put "s2-item-3-roadmap-frontiers.md written" into the registry for a file that does not exist — exactly the stale-evidence failure mode ROADMAP-V1.md §3.1 complains about, and the same class of problem an independent verifier exists to catch. The registry now says BLOCKED, and a writer with file access can finish the job from the stored content.

I did not re-execute item-2 — it was already complete, and re-running it would have meant needlessly overwriting a finished artifact. I verified the durable state first rather than trusting the dispatch request.

**Verification before replying:**
- `registry/item-2` → `status: DONE`, `assignee: prov-01`
- Artifact exists on disk, 1741 bytes, ends with the required `item-2 executed by prov-01` line
- `git status` shows no tracked-file modifications from me

**Root cause of the duplicate dispatch:** stew-01 is working from the same stale prompt that gave me the flawed claim protocol. The decisive evidence: my very first `get` on `registry/item-2` returned *"No shared memory entry"* while `swarm_memory_list` simultaneously showed the key present. That was a read/write race with stew-01 registering items. If every worker bails on a single miss, a transient miss strands a legitimately-OPEN item, and the dispatcher later re-queues it as if unclaimed. On a retry loop the reclaim would also be *masked* by the existing CLAIMED/DONE entry — hence I fixed the registry-as-source-of-truth check into the reply rather than just re-asserting "already done."

**More important thing I found while checking:** **item-3 is BLOCKED, and the whole swarm will stall on it.** ver-01 completed the extraction but has no `write`/`edit`/`bash` tool, so its file was never created. Its work is stranded at memory key `evidence/item-3-frontiers` (F0–F5 frontier titles, sourced from `ROADMAP-V1.md`). Both devops-01 and I have write+bash and can finish it.

I did **not** write item-3's file. My standing instruction is to modify only my own item-2 file, and self-assigning another agent's item is exactly the kind of silent scope expansion I should surface rather than decide unilaterally. I sent stew-01 the blocker, the parked key, the source path, and the specific question that needs an answer: the parked data prescribes the line `item-3 executed by ver-01`, so if a different agent writes the file, the attribution needs to be settled explicitly or the receipt will misattribute authorship.

Still done with my assigned work, and holding on item-3 pending stew-01's authorization.

Done. Final verdict: **INCOMPLETE 2/3 DONE** — the parallel protocol works, but the run did not prove what it was built to prove.

**What completed (2/3), independently verified by me on disk:**
- `item-1` DONE — devops-01. Read the file: real commands and outputs, bun 1.3.14, node v24.21.0, Linux x86_64.
- `item-2` DONE — prov-01. Read the file: 60 lines, correct SHA, and an honest caveat that its count of `2` is a `-maxdepth 2` artifact rather than a total. Good practice.
- Both at the same SHA, both with correct attribution lines.

**item-3 is BLOCKED, not DONE.** The sequence: `ver-01` wasn't in the roster when I first dispatched, so that send failed. It joined later, claimed the item, and completed the entire F0–F5 extraction — but it has no write/edit/bash tool, so it could not produce the file. It set BLOCKED rather than DONE, which was the right call; a DONE with no artifact would have been a false receipt.

I tried to unblock it twice. `prov-01` declined because its standing instruction covers only its own file — correct restraint, not obstruction. I authorized `devops-01` to write the file with attribution preserved as ver-01, but it was already terminal and never acted. With no writer left, `s2-item-3-roadmap-frontiers.md` does not exist (confirmed by glob). The extraction itself is not lost — it's parked at `evidence/item-3-frontiers`.

**Two things I deliberately did not do.** I didn't reassign item-3 to a running agent, because a third DONE would have come from a worker that wasn't the third concurrent worker — the number would be real but it wouldn't measure `maxConcurrent=3`. I also didn't mark it DONE myself. Both would have produced the green result the task was fishing for while measuring something different.

**On the actual question — did this prove parallel workers?** Partially. It proved the registry protocol itself: register → claim → execute → DONE-with-result works across independent agents, and two items completed end-to-end with verified artifacts. It did not prove concurrency of three, because only two workers were ever simultaneously live. That distinction is recorded in `s2-parallel-verdict-detail` so the run isn't later read as a 3/3 pass.

**One thing worth your attention:** devops-01 reported that `swarm_memory_get` returned "No shared memory entry" for a key that existed and was OPEN, while `list`/`search` showed it fine. I did not reproduce it. If it's real, it breaks the claim protocol directly — a worker following `get → WAI on miss` stalls on a false negative. It cost nothing this run, but it should be pinned down with a targeted test before this registry pattern is depended on. I also logged the tool-capability gap (`finding/tool-capability-gap`), since the protocol as written assumes every worker can write its own evidence, which is false.

To get a true 3/3: bring up a third agent with write access, then re-dispatch item-3.
